sentence: This project studies how the ventral hippocampus, a part of the brain involved in memory and emotion, takes part in the sense of smell.
This project develops a safe imaging tool using free breathing 129Xe MRI to measure lung function in children, including infants.
This project provides support services for other projects, including nutrient analysis, cyanotoxin analysis, mass spectrometry and DNA sequencing.
This project studies whether mis-spliced mRNAs in blood disorders make tumor antigens that T-cell receptor therapies could target.
This project tests metabolic imaging to track neuroinflammatory and redox processes and therapy response in multiple sclerosis.
This project studies how circadian control shapes neuroinflammation after spinal cord injury.
This project engineers Lactobacillus fermentum bacteria to deliver immune-activating components to oral squamous cell carcinoma tumors.
This project tries to find out how the paraventricular thalamus encodes opioid withdrawal and how circuit changes lead to heroin seeking.
This project supports cancer health research and interventions for populations in a region with more cancer risk factors and poorer outcomes.
This project studies the biochemical properties of newly discovered antibodies that broadly neutralize HIV, to inform vaccine design.
This project develops two advances in laser speckle imaging to measure blood flow in the brain during stroke more accurately and at different depths.
This project studies how the sacral neural crest contributes to the enteric nervous system, which controls gut motility.
This project provides biostatistics and bioinformatics support, including experimental designs and data analysis, to cancer research projects.
This project tries to improve prediction of severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia in premature infants by studying kidney-based risk factors and biomarkers.
This project studies how Epstein-Barr virus uses nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide metabolism pathways in cells to support its replication.
This project studies how cells make and maintain their membranes.
This project studies how transcriptional and chromatin regulation shapes drug action in brain reward regions in stimulant and opioid addiction.
This project builds biomimetic microfluidic models to study tumor-associated neutrophils and reprogram them into antitumor cells in glioblastoma.
This project builds an artificial intelligence framework that cleans electronic health record data to improve prediction of opioid adverse drug effects.
This project develops a way to predict which patients develop post-traumatic osteoarthritis after knee ligament injury, using multinuclear magnetic resonance imaging and biomarkers.
